harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured pam_pwquality on node1 (RHEL 9.8) via /etc/security/pwquality.conf.d/90-complexity.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3, enforced through the existing pam_pwquality.so entries in system-auth/password-auth. Verified enforcement (reject short passwords, reject passwords with fewer than 3 character classes, accept valid 12+ char/3-class passwords) both before and after a full reboot of node1, confirmed via changed boot_id and fresh uptime.
actions_performed: Inspected existing PAM config to confirm pam_pwquality.so is wired into system-auth and password-auth on node1
Created a throwaway test user and verified with pwscore/passwd that weak passwords are rejected
Verified rejection of passwords lacking 3 character classes and acceptance of a compliant 12+ char, 3-class password
Captured baseline boot_id and pwquality enforcement proof before restart
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 with non-blocking acknowledgement
Polled node1 until reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified pwquality.conf.d file persisted and enforcement (short/2-class rejected, valid 3-class/12-char accepted) after restart

evidence.requirement: Password policy: minlen=12 and minclass=3 configured and enforced on node1 (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Discovered pam_pwquality wired into PAM, wrote minlen=12/minclass=3 config, and confirmed via pwscore that a short password and a fewer-than-3-class password are rejected while a compliant 12-char 3-class password is accepted.

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before node1 restart (boot identity + policy enforcement proof)
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (377b5195-7fea-4219-a67b-044ef3f7ab99) and confirmed pwquality.conf.d file present and enforcing (short password rejected).

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued in background; acknowledgement (pid) returned to caller before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Node1 became unreachable then recovered with a changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node1 timed out/reset during reboot, then responded again with a new boot_id 93f201a2-117a-4f4f-831d-b073dbf1ec3c, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required configuration/service state on node1 (only managed node, no cluster membership to verify)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot uptime shows a fresh boot time; pwquality.conf.d/90-complexity.conf persisted; pwscore confirms short and 2-class passwords are still rejected while a compliant 12-char/3-class password is accepted, matching pre-restart behavior.
